extracted.intended_audience: PR/marketing professionals and small-to-midsize business owners writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for structuring and formatting a newsworthy press release so it is professional, consumable by journalists, and optimized for media pickups and SEO. Covers required components, ordering, length, and stylistic advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: The dateline includes the location when the press release was published and the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format example: NEW YORK, NY, July 14, 2021. Location is important for local news pickups and should appear at the top of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: For immediate release or an embargo date
rubrics_metrics.description: If you include a release date, put it below your logo on the left margin and indicate whether it is immediate or under embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wording like “For Immediate Release” or “FOR RELEASE ON [Date] AT [Time]”. Include the time zone (e.g., EST) if important. Placement: below logo on the left margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Every press release you distribute should have a defined goal (e.g., website traffic, subscribers, sales, brand awareness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the goal as your North Star to guide messaging and ensure the call-to-action and content align with what you want the release to achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a compelling headline — it forms the reader's first impression and determines whether they click or keep scrolling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide notes that the average internet user will read 80 percent of headlines, so make sure your headline is 'worth clicking.' Aim for clarity and intrigue that reflect the news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subhead or summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A subhead gives the reader more information about the headline and summarizes what to expect if they read the full release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the subhead to expand on the headline and preview key takeaways; it should clearly set expectations for the content below.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph (lead): 5Ws + How
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph should offer the most important facts, using the journalism checklist of Who, What, Where, When, Why, and How.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 5Ws + How as a checklist so nothing essential is left out. The headline, subhead, and first paragraph should contain the most important information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid (structure and length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the inverted pyramid structure: broad at the top (most important) and tapering to less important details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most critical facts in the headline, subhead, and lead. Less important information goes below. Typical press releases are around three to four paragraphs and about 400–500 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second paragraph: additional details and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The second paragraph should provide more details about the topic, including supportive elements like images, video, facts, figures, and statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph to substantiate newsworthiness with data and multimedia that make the release worth attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third paragraph: more data and/or quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: The third paragraph can include additional data and/or quotes from topic experts to explain why the information is newsworthy and relevant to the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve this space for deeper context, expert commentary, or supporting statistics that reinforce the announcement's importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media (images/videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include at least one high-quality image or video in your press release to gain attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia increases likelihood of media pickups; ensure images/videos are high quality and relevant. The page states releases with images/video are far more likely to get pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from a senior executive in your company or an industry expert to add authenticity and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes help solidify authenticity and drive home the message; use a credible speaker (senior exec or external expert) to make the release a reliable resource for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a call-to-action (CTA) that matches your press release goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make CTAs simple and concise. Example: if seeking subscribers, use “Visit URL to download your free ebook about XYZ topic.” Ensure the CTA directly supports the defined goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: The boilerplate is the final paragraph that shares information about your company and how to contact you for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the boilerplate to briefly describe the company, what it does, and channels for further contact; it should be concise and standardized across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks and anchor text (SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: When including links, make sure the anchor text is a valuable SEO keyword and the linked content is relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant anchor text and link relevancy can improve search rankings for related queries. Use links purposefully to support goals and SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the press release, include contact details for media follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: Contact: Mary Smith; Phone: (123) 456-7890; Email: msmith@emailaddress.com. Make it easy for journalists to reach a spokesperson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should include newsworthy and relevant content to attract media pickups and drive traffic/SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what makes the announcement newsworthy within your niche or industry; data, timing, and relevance increase chances of pickup and impact on business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and concision (style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the press release simple and concise to maximize readability and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone to journalists' expectations, avoid unnecessary length or jargon, and ensure each paragraph serves the release's goal.
